subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Fixed in one’s ways

options.text: An aggressive attack on someone by a group
Not willing or wanting to change from your normal way of doing something
Something that shows potential or looks promising in the beginning but fails to deliver anything in the end

solution:
The correct answer is "**Not willing or wanting to change from your normal way of doing something.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"Fixed in one's ways" means being stubborn or resistant to change.** (जिद्दी)
 
• The idiom suggests that someone has established a routine or method of doing things and is unwilling to deviate from it.
 
• This can be seen as a negative trait, as it may prevent someone from adapting to new situations or ideas.
 
 
• Example: "My grandfather is fixed in his ways and refuses to use a smartphone, even though it would make his life easier."
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.
